title: Khao Man Gai
subtitle: Thai poached chicken with rice cooked in broth
excerpt: Khao man gai is Thailand's take on Hainanese chicken rice. The chicken is gently poached until silky, and the resulting broth cooks the rice. It is a quiet, restorative dish with great depth from simple ingredients.
sourceNotes: Based on Thai street-food tradition. The technique of cooking rice in poaching broth is shared across Thai, Singaporean, and Chinese variants.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Poach the chicken a few hours ahead. Keep in the broth until ready to serve.

content.text: Using chicken breasts here gives tender, easy-to-slice results. The key is a gentle simmer, never a boil. If you have a rice cooker, use it for the broth rice.

items.prepNote: 2 whole for poaching, 2 sliced to serve

content.text: Put the stock, ginger, garlic, and 2 whole spring onions into the stockpot. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the chicken breasts. Keep the heat low so the broth barely bubbles. Poach for 18 to 20 minutes until cooked through.
Lift the chicken out. Set aside to rest. Keep the broth warm on low heat.
Measure 480ml of the warm broth. Use it to cook the rice in a saucepan or rice cooker.
While the rice cooks, mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small dish for the dipping sauce.
Slice the rested chicken thinly across the grain.
Serve rice in bowls, topped with sliced chicken and cucumber. Add a small bowl of the remaining hot broth on the side. Offer the dipping sauce and sliced spring onion.

items.cause: Heat was too high or it poached too long
items.fix: Keep the broth at a gentle shimmer, not a boil.
Use full-strength stock, not watered-down broth.

items.cause: Using dark soy instead of light
items.fix: Use light soy sauce only and taste before serving.
